hook.text: Everyone kept telling me: learn with AI. So I did. And then I tried… with maths.

problem.text: Before I can even ask my question, I have to retype every equation. The AI can't see my screen. It can't point. And it just hands me the answer. No wonder maths scores are at a historic low.

meet.text: So I built Gerald. The AI teacher that lives on your screen. It sees. It talks. It draws. And it makes you think.

demo1.text: Hold a key, and just talk. Your worksheet is already on screen. I make the classic mistake, and Gerald stops me, and points at the exercise, instead of giving the answer.

demo2.text: I write on the board, by hand. Gerald follows every line, underlines the sign error in red, and lets me fix it. Only then does it write the clean solution.

demo3.text: Ask for the parabola, and it plots the real curve: roots, vertex, live, right where you work.

demo4.text: Same engine, any software. In Photoshop, I ask for a red square. Gerald points at Shapes, then Rectangle, then the fill colour and the hex code, and waits for my click at every step. By the end, I don't just have a red square: I know the tool. Photoshop today, Excel or Figma tomorrow. Gerald points. You click. You learn.

agents.text: Now, the market. Clicky, Claude computer use, OpenAI's agent: brilliant, but they're assistants. They take the mouse and do the task for you. You learn nothing. ChatGPT and Gemini are stuck in a chat box. Gerald is different: it's a teacher. It sees your work, shows you exactly where, writes on it, and lets you try first.

numbers.text: Zero equations retyped. Thirty-seven times more precise pointing. Half a second to find any target. Pedagogy score from seventy-seven to ninety-three percent. All for a fraction of a cent.

cta.text: Stop retyping. Stop screenshotting. Just ask Gerald. The first teacher you can actually mute.
